identity.title: Molecular Gas Properties in M83 from CO PDFs

paper_type_evidence.quote: We have obtained $^{12}$CO(1–0) data of the nearby barred spiral galaxy M83 from Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array and Nobeyama 45m observations.

redshift_or_distance.value: nearby; 2'' ~ 40 pc (distance value not stated explicitly)

evidence.quote: a high angular resolution ($2''$ corresponding to $\sim 40$ pc at the distance of M83) has been achieved.
a high angular resolution ($2''$ corresponding to $\sim 40$ pc at the distance of M83) has been achieved.

question.value: How do galactic structures (center, bar, arm) and stellar feedback affect the PDFs of CO integrated intensity, peak temperature and velocity dispersion in M83?

evidence.quote: In order to investigate how these galactic structures affect gas properties, we have created a probability distribution function (PDF) of the CO integrated intensity ($I_{\rm CO}$), peak temperature, and velocity dispersion for a region with each structure.
The data have been obtained for the Cycle 0 project 2011.0.00772.S,
We have mapped a central disk area of M83 in the $^{12}$CO(1–0) emission using Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) and the Nobeyama 45m telescope (NRO45m).
We have obtained $^{12}$CO(1–0) data of the nearby barred spiral galaxy M83

configurations.value: 2 EBs compact, 3 EBs extended; 45 mosaic pointings

evidence.quote: consist of two Execution Blocks (EBs) with a compact configuration and three EBs with an extended configuration.
The synthesized beam is $2.0''\times 1.1''$ in full width at half maximum.

sensitivity.value: 8.0 mJy/beam (0.33 K) per 2.6 km/s channel; moment-0 1σ 47 mJy/beam km/s (1.8 K km/s)

evidence.quote: We adopt a $1\sigma$ sensitivity of each channel to be 8.0 mJy/beam or 0.33 K with a channel width of 2.6 km/s.

provided.value: Single-dish CO(1-0) OTF map combined with ALMA to recover total flux

evidence.quote: By combining these two data sets, the total CO flux has been recovered

what.value: Catalogs of young star clusters, HII regions and SNRs used to define feedback areas

evidence.quote: A feedback area and non-feedback area are defined according to catalogs of HII regions, young star clusters, and SNRs.

external_data_from_literature.citation: not specified in text (reference list includes Blair12, Blair14, Whit11, Dop10)

what.value: Bar radial range from Ks-band Fourier analysis

evidence.quote: we define the radial range of the bar to be $r=20''$–$85''$.
The pixel size is set to be $0.25''$.

evidence.quote: Then, the two uv data sets from ALMA and NRO45m are Fourier-transformed and deconvolved together.
The synthesized beam is $2.0''\times 1.1''$ in full width at half maximum.
A detail of observations and data reduction will be in paper I, and we provide a summary here.

method.value: PDFs of I_CO, T_peak, σ_V for center, bar (r=20''-85'', semi-minor 46'') and arm regions

evidence.quote: The semi-minor axis of the bar is set to be $46''$ based on an ellipse fitting to the same $K_{\rm s}$-band image.

validation.value: Tested center outer boundary at r=10'' and 30''

evidence.quote: We have confirmed that this general trend holds when the outer boundary of the center region is changed to $r=10''$ or $30''$.

method.value: Feedback area within 2'' of young clusters, HII regions or SNRs; compare PDFs, fit bright-end slopes at Σ>10^3 Msun/pc2 with a line

evidence.quote: we fit each PDF at $\Sigma > 10^3~M_\odot/{\rm pc^2} = 6\times 10^{22}~{\rm H_2/cm^2}$ with a line.

fitting.value: linear fit to bright end; slopes consistent within errors

evidence.quote: slopes of the two fitted lines ( lines in Figure [4](#fig:Ico_fb)) are consistent within errors.
The synthesized beam is $2.0''\times 1.1''$ in full width at half maximum.
A typical $1\sigma$ sensitivity of the integrated intensity map is estimated to be 47 mJy/beam km/s or 1.8 K km/s.
Peak positions of bar and arm PDFs are similar (10–30 K km/s), while that for center is an order of magnitude higher.
the bar PDF exhibits a PL like tail at the bright end ($I_{\rm CO} \ensuremath{\gtrsim} 100$ K km/s).

findings_qualitative.value: σ_V PDF for the bar is shifted to larger values than for the arm; T_peak PDFs similar

evidence.quote: While $T_{\rm peak}$ PDFs do not differ between the bar and arm regions, the $\sigma_V$ PDF for the bar is shifted to the right-hand side of that for the arm.

claims.hypothesis: Does the bar I_CO PDF bright-end tail indicate active star formation as in the MW?
claims.experiment: Compare I_CO PDFs of bar and arm regions
claims.result: Bar shows PL-like tail at I_CO≳100 K km/s; arm does not, although SFE is lower in the bar
claims.finding: At 40 pc scale a bright-end tail is not always a sign of active star formation

evidence.quote: This result indicates that at least at 40 pc scale the $I_{\rm CO}$ tail is not always a sign of active star formation.

claims.hypothesis: Stellar feedback explains the PDF differences between bar and arm
claims.experiment: Compare PDFs in feedback vs non-feedback areas
claims.result: I_CO and σ_V PDFs do not differ significantly; T_peak shallower in feedback area
claims.finding: Feedback does not explain the bar-arm difference at this scale

evidence.quote: We thus conclude that at least at 40 pc scale the feedback effect does not explain the different PDFs between bar and arm regions.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Stellar feedback truncating the arm PDF considered and found not dominant

evidence.quote: Another explanation for the different $I_{\rm CO}$ PDFs is that the arm PDF is truncated due to the effect of stellar feedback

limitations_admitted.value: Few data points above the density limit; constant X_CO assumed

evidence.quote: Although the number of data points that exceed this gas density limit is small

referee_caveats_inferred: PDF shapes depend on uv coverage, noise and moment-map method; no tests shown
Constant X_CO may bias I_CO PDFs between bar and arm
Feedback area definition (2'' radius) is arbitrary
